title: Godot Voxel engine
author: chauquest
selftext:
Hello, this is a post that belonged to r/VoxelGameDev, but they don't accept any AI-assisted coding, so screw them.



I am making a voxel engine for Godot using direct compute shaders, and I picked the work back up because I needed to make a transition at the end of v2 that required a lot of code refactoring (to erase the CPU bottleneck). LLMs also became strong enough for this kind of task. I just want to share the progress with you. Everything is open source, so you can take inspiration from the architecture. The architecture is still human-decided; the implementation is largely AI, which I still need to proofread.



I managed to trick Godot into linking the mesher (math) to the renderer (visual). As I said in the comments of my previous post, I use a pool of MultiMeshes that I basically scatter wherever I need them, which removes any CPU bottleneck on this front.



On top of this I added an instance system (for the trees). Instances have an exact SDF up close and store a density moment for far away. That's why the forest becomes a green blob: far away, all the instances are just leaf density moments merging together. The biome system is a bit less polished and uses a bit too much compute right now...



Every SDF in the world sits on a "wavelength band", which defines its influence. This means a LOD 0 chunk only computes 32\^3 at LOD 0, 16\^3 at LOD 1, ..., capped at 8\^3 for everything coarser. Right now there are 25 LODs for 25 bands. The world uses int64 chunk coordinates, with 32x32x32 chunks of 5 cm voxels at LOD 0. I also added a capsule and a 10 cm sphere to the instance types, which I use to carve details in the demo.



However, performance-wise it is not so bright. I am running everything on a laptop 3060, mainly with two tricks: FSR2 x2 upscaling, and on top of that a nearest-pixel x2 upscale. Basically, I render the game at 1/4 of the resolution to get 60 FPS.



The scene rendered is an infinite biome land with a forest of 1M trees on top. Each tree is an individual instance, so you can imagine harvesting them.



The engine is still publicly available on \[my GitHub\](https://github.com/aobayama-gaming/opti-voxel).



Nice coding to everyone
